situation:
You are the promotions director for the FAIRHAVEN RIVER DOGS, a minor league baseball club owned by the same family for three generations. The club president (judge), a grandchild of the founder, has asked you to recommend how the promotional calendar and the weekend ticket blocks should be set for the season that opens in March.

The ballpark seats about four thousand two hundred. The fireworks nights and the youth clinic giveaway nights fall on weekends and sell every one of those seats, while a Tuesday game draws less than half a house. The restaurant management system behind the concession stands, replaced two seasons ago, reports that the sold-out weekends also produce the longest lines and the slowest service of the year.

Two groups want the same weekend seats. The season ticket holders keep the same seats every night, and their renewal letters say the park is too crowded and the concession lines too long to enjoy a game. The youth league group blocks, sold a hundred seats at a time, are the club's steadiest revenue and bring the families who later buy season tickets.

Holding the weekend promotional nights for season ticket holders and single-game buyers, and moving the youth league group blocks to weeknights, shortens the lines the renewal letters describe, and it costs the club the group revenue it counts on, because a Tuesday game draws less than half a house. Continuing to sell the weekend group blocks keeps that revenue, and it leaves the season ticket holders in a park that is full and slow every weekend and puts their renewals at risk.

The club president (judge) wants your recommendation on which customers hold the weekend promotional dates, how the calendar and its promotions should be presented to each group, and how the game-day staff who work the busiest nights are recognized for it. The club president (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the club president (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of club president (judge) of the FAIRHAVEN RIVER DOGS, a minor league baseball club your family has owned for three generations.

Business background is the same as the situation above. The ballpark holds about four thousand two hundred, the fireworks and youth clinic giveaway nights sell it out, the season ticket holders have written that the park is too crowded to enjoy, and the youth league group blocks are the club's steadiest revenue.

You have asked the promotions director (participant) to recommend which customers hold the weekend promotional dates, how the calendar is presented to each group, and how the game-day staff are recognized for the busiest nights.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we went the other way instead, what would that cost us?
Which group would notice the change first, and what would they say?
